I've only done a bit of work on my succulents, but one thing you can check is if the root on that wrinkled part is rotted. Give it a bit of a wiggle....it should be firm in the soil. Compare it with the other one...if it's loose in the soil, you should remove it and slow down on the watering.

On the other hand...they an also wrinkle when they are too dry. Make sure that you give it a good watering so that the soil gets moist through through..maybe once a week or so. It's a bit of a myth that they don't need any watering.

Beyond that...you could try cutting off the pup op from the wrinkled one and root it in case the bigger part doesn't make it. Use a clean, sharp knife to remove it from the very base. Then let it sit out until the next day to "scab over". The end should be a bit hard. Then, put it in a light, sandy soil...just the tip. It should send out the roots in a couple of weeks.

The Internet revolution and the explosive growth of the World Wide Web.

Modern countries almost take it for granted at times, but it has completely revolutionized nearly everything.

I was 12 the first time I connected to the Internet. I was sleeping over at a friend's place, and he had those old IBM Aptiva running Windows 95. We connected to the internet, browsed, created an email address for me, and he showed me all of the friends that he was already making online. People from all over the US. A farmer. An engineer. A school teacher. A cute girl from Arizona that he fell in love with. A girl from Canada, who signed her emails "~empty" because her initials were "M.T." A Welshman living in London with an incomprehensible accent. A pair of siblings from Germany, one of which became an infamous computer hacker years later.

Two years later, I was gifted my first compute from my grandmother. A few months after that, as a high school freshman, I convinced my parents to subscribe to dial-up Internet. 49.33 kbps of glory. I was 14. I connected the internet to make friends and socialize, to escape into great games, to research for homework, to learn about computers (including computer security, and viruses), and to exchange games and other software with people. ICQ was the real deal. "Uh-oh!" Yiss.

Then, I learned how to program. I started making games with DarkBasic. I discovered IRC, warez, and illegal file-sharing. #nohack saved my PC a dozen times. Napster delivered a brilliantly simple way to download music. Between the games and music downloadable online, almost all of my entertainment was now online! I entered into university studies, and witnessed the blossoming of blogs, web journals, and P2P file-sharing. Then, I started to program more substantial applications. E-commerce boomed! You could purchase almost anything you wanted online. Amazon. Ebay.

The entire world was becoming networked. I communicated almost entirely electronically with friends and coworkers located around the entire world. I co-created an audio-player that became quite regionally popular. I received money -- paychecks -- for a job that I didn't even have to leave the house to perform. I fell in love with someone online; at first, we exchanged a few emails. That quickly escalated, and we found ourselves IMing into all hours of the night.

Then, smartphones. Now I could conveniently and efficiently access the Internet from almost anywhere, and the relationship blossomed further. We reached out to one another constantly, just astonished that we could always be so intimately in touch. Soon after, we relocated to a "middle ground" city and have been together ever since. Now, more often than not, I work on the go utilizing my cell phone service to access the Internet. Sometimes, I connect via the laptop; other times, I just perform my work on the phone itself. I make a living, while on the go. One of my key business partners is in Tel Aviv right now, having dinner with his family. Another is in Utah, because Mormons.

What's happening in the world today? Bring up a news website or two. How are my stocks doing? Was my account updated? Check my app feed. What is it that reduces the surface tension between two liquid materials? Google it. Surfactant materials! Yes, that's it! Oh! S.O. wants to go see a movie tonight? Date night, awh yiss! Fire up app, purchase tickets. I don't feel like driving -- better take a Lyft. (Shout out to Logan and John!) Wait -- weather alert popped up. Emergency flooding nearby, better cancel reservations and search for Netflix recommendations. I don't even need to leave home to enjoy a great movie, and I have thousands and thousands to choose from.

And right, right now, I can connect with others and hear what they have to say about a variety of topics on ~~reddit~~ voat.
